annotationRationale: Sign changes and endpoint inclusion constrain root multiplicities. Factorization and cancellation identify duplicate representations, while original domains distinguish functions with an extra excluded input. Addition combines the two disjoint families.
sourceMethod: Followed the official MAA argument on pages 19 and 20: place the third numerator root at c, d, or e and count 5 + 3 functions. Clarified equality of domains in the first two cases and the retained excluded input in the third.

review.mathCheck: The four sign-changing endpoints force simple numerator roots a,b. Choosing four ordered endpoints gives five reduced quotients. Placing the remaining numerator root at c or d yields the same function; placing it at e gives three additional functions whose extra excluded input lies outside both required intervals. Thus 5+3=8, absent from the choices; historical E=13 is incorrect.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, independently worded adaptation of official Q25, pages 19-20. It preserves the multiplicity cases and 5+3 count, while explicitly justifying duplicate representations, original domains and distinct functions.
